title: The multiplication table
prompt:
Print the `n`-by-`n` multiplication table, rows of `row * col` padded into neat columns. The starter reads `n`.

The shape is two nested loops: an outer loop over rows, an inner loop over columns, a `mul` in the middle, and a newline after each row. The cell format `%4lld` right-aligns every product into a four-character column so the table lines up.

`printf` is free to overwrite `x9` through `x15`, so keep both counters in `row_r` and `col_r`. The starter gives those names to `x19` and `x20`, which `printf` must hand back unchanged.

## What is checked

- four rows of four aligned products for the `4` in the stdin box
- the program exits cleanly
- the products come from `mul` inside the loops
- the same holds for other sizes you do not see, down to a one-by-one table
starter:
// print an n-by-n multiplication table
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(row_r, x19)
define(col_r, x20)
define(cell_r, x21)
define(n_r, x22)

        .data
fmt_in:     .string "%lld"
fmt_cell:   .string "%4lld"
fmt_eol:     .string "\n"

        .bss
        .balign 8
n_m:        .skip 8

        .text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        ldr     x0, =fmt_in                 // read the table's size
        ldr     x1, =n_m
        bl      scanf
        ldr     x9, =n_m
        ldr     n_r, [x9]

        // TODO: two nested loops, rows and columns each running 1 to
        // n. Print row * col with fmt_cell for every column, then
        // print fmt_eol at the end of each row. Keep both counters in
        // the aliased callee-saved registers: printf owns the scratch
        // ones while it runs.

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
